1.explanation:
• lib/features/rules/BpmnRules.js: This is where we enforce model rules (canCreate, canDrop, canReplace). We need to add a check that disallows creating or moving Start Events with any eventDefinition into a non-event Sub Process.  
• lib/features/replace/BpmnReplace.js: This handles the copy/replace of business objects, including eventDefinitions. When moving or morphing a Start Event into a Sub Process, we must drop the eventDefinitionType from the target so that the resulting Start Event is untyped.  
• lib/features/popup-menu/ReplaceMenuProvider.js: This builds the replace (morph) menu. We must filter out typed Start Event options when the current element’s parent is a Sub Process, so users can’t morph to a typed Start Event inside it.  
• lib/features/replace/ReplaceOptions.js: This defines the available replace targets (including all typed and untyped Start Events). We should scope or prune the typed Start Event entries when in the context of a non-event Sub Process so that they never appear as replace options in that context.
1.bug_scenario: A user is allowed to morph or drag a typed start event (for example, a Message Start Event) into a non-event-based Sub Process. In the provided GIF, the user drops the message start event into the expanded Sub Process and ends up with a plain circle, but the palette still shows typed start events and the replace menu will allow morphing to a typed start event inside a Sub Process. According to BPMN rules, any Start Event inside a non-event Sub Process must be untyped (no event definitions) and the user must not be allowed to choose a typed event there.
